nodes.name: One-step hydrothermal V-Ni3S2 growth
nodes.procedure: V-Ni3S2 nanorod arrays are grown on commercial nickel foam (NF) by a one-step hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: Fig. 1 shows the synthetic process... Firstly, V·Ni3S2 nanorod arrays are grown on commercial nickel foam (NF) by a one-step hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: Fast electrodeposition NiFe LDH
nodes.procedure: NiFe LDH nanosheets are directly electrodeposited on the V·Ni3S2 nanorod arrays to form the unique 3D core–shell V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH catalyst. The optimal electrodeposition time is 80 s.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: NiFe LDH nanosheets are directly electrodeposited on the V·Ni3S2 nanorod arrays... the catalyst with electrodeposition time of 80 s exhibits the highest OER activity

nodes.source_text: Then NiFe LDH nanosheets are directly electrodeposited on the V·Ni3S2 nanorod arrays... we also studied the morphology variation... with different electrodeposition time of NiFe LDH, and the catalyst with electrodeposition time of 80 s exhibits the highest OER activity

nodes.source_text: The OER performance of as-prepared catalysts was evaluated by a three-electrode system in 1 M KOH electrolyte at room temperature... V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH catalyst only needs 209 mV to deliver 10 mA cm−2... 286 mV at 100 mA cm−2... Tafel slope of 32.5 mV dec−1... Cdl value of 32.6 mF cm−2... charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 3.6 Ω
the V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH catalyst requires overpotentials of 120 and 222 mV to drive current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2, respectively

the V-Ni3S2 electrode delivers current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2 at overpotentials as low as 91 and 170 mV, respectively... the V-Ni3S2 also shows a relatively smaller Tafel slope of 72.8 mV dec−1

nodes.description: Overall water splitting V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH(+)/V-Ni3S2(-) in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: we combined our novel core–shell V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH catalyst (anode) with the V-Ni3S2 nanorod arrays (cathode) to assemble a two-electrode electrolyzer for overall water splitting in 1 M KOH... cell voltages to obtain current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2 are 1.55 and 1.77 V... Faraday efficiency is close to 100%... exhibits good stability during 24 h long-term stability test

nodes.description: OER stability testing in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: a long-term water oxidation durability test was carried out at constant current densities... the core–shell V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH shows good stability both under current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2 without significant degradation

nodes.description: HER stability testing in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the overpotentials at current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm−2 have no drastic increase during long-time stability tests, demonstrating the good HER stability of V-Ni3S2 nanorod arrays

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows V-Ni3S2 nanorods with ~120 nm diameter decorated with NiFe LDH nanosheets forming 3D core-shell nanostructure with rough surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Fig. 2a, b and S2†) of V-Ni3S2 show a typical 1D nanorod array morphology, and the average diameter of the nanorod is about 120 nm. After decoration of NiFe LDH nanosheets... forming a unique 3D core–shell nanostructure with a very rough surface (Fig. 2c and d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals core-shell structure with ~120 nm V-Ni3S2 core and ~150 nm NiFe LDH shell; NiFe LDH nanosheets are interconnected providing channels for electrolyte diffusion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image in Fig. 2e further exhibits the core–shell nanostructures with ∼120 nm core of V-Ni3S2 nanorods and ∼150 nm shell of NiFe LDH nanosheets...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows ultrathin NiFe LDH nanosheets ~2.4 nm thick (three monolayers) with (012) plane spacing of 0.25 nm and numerous defects indicated by arrows.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Fig. 2f reveals that the thickness of the ultrathin NiFe LDH nanosheets is ∼2.4 nm, indicating three monolayers... In Fig. 2g, the HRTEM image shows typical (012) plane of NiFe LDH with an interplanar spacing of 0.25 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX line scan and elemental mapping confirm V-doping and core-shell structure with S centralized in V-Ni3S2 core and Fe in outer NiFe LDH shell; atomic ratio S:Ni:V:Fe ≈ 1:1.73:0.04:0.29.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) line scanning results (Fig. 2h) and elemental mapping images (Fig. 2i) further confirm the success of V doping and the core–shell nanostructure... Fig. S5† shows the TEM EDX spectrum... atomic ratio is about 1:1.73:0.04:0.29.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns indexed to heazlewoodite Ni3S2 (JCPDF no. 44-1418) and Ni (JCPDF no. 04-0580); no significant NiFe LDH peaks due to ultrathin, defect-rich nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As expected, from the XRD patterns in Fig. 3a, all peaks are well indexed to heazlewoodite Ni3S2 (JCPDF no. 44-1418) and Ni (JCPDF no. 04-0580) after hydrothermal treatment of Ni foam. After decoration of NiFe LDH nanosheets, no significant diffraction peak of NiFe LDH was detected...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows NiFe LDH peaks at 460, 550, 680 cm^-1 and Ni3S2 characteristic peaks at 188, 198, 286, 222, 323, 349 cm^-1 confirming both phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3b, six Raman peaks at 188, 198, 286, 222, 323, and 349 cm-1 are the characteristic peaks of Ni3S2 phase... NiFe LDH has three typical broad peaks at about 460, 550, and 680 cm-1.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows S 2p peaks at 161.9 eV (S-S), 163.4 eV (S-Ni/S-V), 168.6 eV (S-O); V 2p peaks at 514.3, 515.6, 516.5, 522.4, 524.0 eV indicate V^4+ and V^5+ states; Fe 2p at 712.8/725.6 eV; Ni 2p shift from 855.6/873.5 eV (V-Ni3S2) to 856.3/874.3 eV (V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH) indicates strong electronic interaction between core and shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 3c of high-resolution XPS spectra of S 2p, the two 2p3/2 peaks at 168.6 and 161.9 eV correspond to the S–O and S–S, and the metal–sulfur bindings of S–Ni and S–V are overlapped in the position around 163.4 eV. The high-resolution V 2p spectrum can be decomposed to five peaks at 514.3, 515.6, 516.5, 522.4, and 524.0 eV... the two peaks at 712.8 and 725.6 eV in the high-resolution Fe 2p spectrum... the two peaks at 856.3 and 874.3 eV corresponding to Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 for V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH shift positively compared with those (855.6 and 873.5 eV) for V-Ni3S2, implying the strong electronic interactions...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives double-layer capacitance Cdl of 32.6 mF cm^-2 for V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH (1.4x higher than V-Ni3S2 at 23.8 mF cm^-2, 2.2x higher than NiFe LDH at 10.5 mF cm^-2), indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: cyclic voltammetry (CV) tests at different scanning speeds (Fig. S10†) to obtain the doublelayer capacitance (Cdl)... the V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH catalyst exhibits a largest Cdl value of 32.6 mF cm-2 (Fig. 4e), which is about 1.4 times as that of V-Ni3S2 (23.8 mF cm-2) and 2.2 times as that of NiFe LDH (10.5 mF cm-2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots at 250 mV overpotential show smallest charge transfer resistance Rct of 3.6 Ω for V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH vs 4.5 Ω (NiFe LDH) and 3.8 Ω (V-Ni3S2), demonstrating improved conductivity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: electrochemical impedance spectra (EIS) was conducted... As the Nyquist plots shown in Fig. 4f... the 3D core–shell V-Ni3S2@NiFe LDH has a smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 3.6 Ω, as compared to the pure NiFe LDH (4.5 Ω) and V-Ni3S2 (3.8 Ω), demonstrating improved conductivity...
